differences.title: 1. INITIAL LOAD
differences.leftDesc: Reduced JavaScript sent to the client for faster initial page loads.
differences.rightDesc: More JavaScript shipped, potentially leading to longer initial load times.

differences.title: 2. INTERACTIVITY
differences.rightTitle: Directly supports client-side interactivity and state management.
differences.leftDesc: Requires explicit 'use client' for client-side interactivity and state.

differences.title: 3. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Can fetch data directly on the server before rendering.
differences.rightDesc: Must fetch data in the browser using APIs or client hooks.

differences.title: 4. BUNDLE SIZE
differences.leftDesc: Contribute less JavaScript to the client bundle, improving performance.
differences.rightDesc: Increase the client-side JavaScript bundle size significantly.

differences.title: 5. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: No client-side state hooks (like useState, useReducer) available.
differences.rightDesc: Full access to client-side state management hooks and libraries.

differences.title: 6. RERENDERING
differences.leftDesc: Rerendered on the server during the build or server request.
differences.rightDesc: Rerendered in the browser based on state changes or props.

differences.title: 7. ACCESS TO DOM
differences.leftDesc: Cannot directly access the browser's Document Object Model.
differences.rightDesc: Can directly interact with the DOM and browser APIs.
